name: Phoenix Art Museum
funding: Expenses $11.9M (FY2023) plus a $12M endowment fund; trustees, members, City of Phoenix.
watch: Current corporate partner is Desert Diamond Casino (gambling operator). Board chair is the CFO of Pinnacle West (APS), a coal-burning utility.
why_flagged: Current corporate partner is Desert Diamond Casino (gambling operator). Board chair is the CFO of Pinnacle West (APS), a coal-burning utility.
records_note: It posts audits for 2019 to 2025 and Form 990s for 2020 to 2025, names corporate partners by tier and lists about 40 trustees.

name: Pictanovo
watch: Caroline Lang presided over Pictanovo's economic support fund for films and series until 4 February 2026. Pictanovo is an association funded by the Hauts-de-France region.
why_flagged: Regional film agency run as an association. Its economic support fund is paid by the Hauts-de-France region, and public aid is capped at 50% of a work's cost.
records_note: Its site lists the 24-member board in a March 2026 PDF but posts no activity report or accounts; funders show only as logos.

name: Pinacoteca de São Paulo
funding: Maintainer B3; São Paulo state via APAC; Lei Rouanet. Master sponsors Bradesco, InfinitePay, Itaú, Vivo, Chanel. Gold sponsors include Equinor, Ultra, Bloomberg, J.P. Morgan, Motiva.
watch: Equinor is a state-majority oil and gas company and Ultra owns Ipiranga fuel distribution. Both are gold sponsors in the July 2026 panel.
why_flagged: Maintainer B3; São Paulo state via APAC; Lei Rouanet. Master sponsors Bradesco, InfinitePay, Itaú, Vivo, Chanel. Gold sponsors include Equinor, Ultra, Bloomberg, J.P. Morgan, Motiva.
records_note: Operator APAC posts annual reports for 2018 to 2025, audited accounts from 2006 and its council; the sponsor list is a July 2026 image.

name: PinchukArtCentre
funding: Private centre founded in 2006 and run by the Victor Pinchuk Foundation. Pinchuk's fortune comes from Interpipe, a maker of steel pipes and railway wheels.
watch: In 2020 two PinchukArtPrize nominees withdrew with open letters after 28 guides were dismissed. The centre denies the sackings were over their union.
why_flagged: Private centre founded in 2006 by Victor Pinchuk, a project of his foundation. His fortune comes from Interpipe, a steel pipe and railway wheel maker. No sponsors listed.
records_note: No records of its own: its founder's Victor Pinchuk Foundation posts annual reports from 2009 to 2018; the centre lists staff, no funders or board.

name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
funding: Founded and supported by Pirelli, its only named backer; Marco Tronchetti Provera chairs it. Technical sponsors include K-Way and M&C Saatchi Milano.
watch: Industrial contemporary space in Milan with Anselm Kiefer's 'The Seven Heavenly Palaces'. Admission is free; governance is closely tied to Pirelli's corporate sponsorship and executive board oversight.
why_flagged: On 4 June 2026 Grizzly Research alleged Pirelli's Russian plants serve Rostec, a sanctioned group owning 25% of Pirelli Tyre Russia. Pirelli denies it.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the about page names Pirelli as founder, three technical sponsors, and a board with chairman Marco Tronchetti Provera, undated.

name: Poetry in America (Harvard)
watch: Epstein's foundation Gratitude America gave $110,000 in 2016 to Verse Video Education, the nonprofit behind Elisa New's Poetry in America, and New and Epstein emailed about funding her projects from 2013 to at least 2018, including a possible $500,000 donation. Harvard gave the nonprofit office space and paid part of its staff salaries.
why_flagged: Nonprofit Verse Video Education runs it. Elisa New credits the National Endowment for the Humanities and Sloan Foundation for four seasons. Harvard gave office space and part of staff pay.
records_note: The producer, Verse Video Education, posts no reports, funders or board on its site; its Form 990s are on ProPublica.

name: Pritzker Architecture Prize
watch: Tom Pritzker runs the Hyatt Foundation, which is behind the Pritzker Architecture Prize. Unredacted DOJ files show frequent contact with Epstein after his 2008 plea deal.
why_flagged: Founded in 1979 and sponsored by the Pritzker family's Hyatt Foundation. The laureate receives $100,000. No outside sponsors are listed.
records_note: The prize site names only its sponsor, the Hyatt Foundation, whose Form 990-PF filings for 2001 to 2024 are on ProPublica; no reports or board.

name: PRO ARTE Foundation
watch: Vladimir Potanin is on the UK list (June 2022) and the US list (Dec 2022). PRO ARTE has run his foundation's grant competitions since 2016.
why_flagged: St Petersburg charitable foundation. Its 2025 report lists programme backers: the city's Committees for Culture and Social Policy, Friends of BDT Foundation and the Vladimir Potanin Foundation.
records_note: The foundation posts reports and audits for 2023 to 2025, names its five-member board, and its 2025 report lists backers including the Potanin Foundation.

name: Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts
watch: Marina Loshak left in March 2023; Ekaterina Pronicheva is director now. The board of trustees includes Sberbank, Gazprombank, PSB and Transneft.
why_flagged: VTB is general sponsor of the museum, and PSB partnered the Diamond Chariot Buddhist art exhibition. LG and Yandex Eda are also partners.
records_note: The museum posts activity reports and Treasury financial forms for 2012 to 2025, shows four undated sponsor logos, and names its board of trustees.

name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
watch: 2011 naming row, four trustees resigned; Griffin gallery 2024.
why_flagged: 2011 naming row, four trustees resigned; Griffin gallery 2024.
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2024 and its site names donors by tier and trustees; no recent annual reports found.

name: Qatar Museums
watch: Labour abuses documented by HRW in 2026.
why_flagged: Qatari government entity founded in 2005 and chaired by Sheikha Al-Mayassa bint Hamad Al Thani; it oversees the state's museums and heritage sites.
records_note: Qatar Museums posts no annual report or accounts and names no sponsors, but lists its board of eight trustees by name.

name: Raw Material Company
funding: Founded 2008 by Koyo Kouoh. Partners listed for 2024: Arts Collaboratory, OSIWA, Mellon Foundation, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Little Sun, Porticus and Sharjah Art Foundation.
watch: Operates the RAW Académie, a residency and study programme examining trans-African knowledge production and decolonial curatorial practice.
why_flagged: Founded 2008 by Koyo Kouoh. Partners listed for 2024: Arts Collaboratory, OSIWA, Mellon Foundation, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Little Sun, Porticus and Sharjah Art Foundation.
records_note: Site unreachable; its 2024 programme announcement names Arts Collaboratory, Osiwa, Mellon, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Little Sun, Porticus and Sharjah Art Foundation.
